Blip.notes: No published source. Read from the installed 2.0.0 plugin.dylib, which is unstripped: every module's constructor, process and Osc::process carry local symbols, so the figures here are read off the code rather than a manual. There is no manual, no README and no res/ documentation; the folder holds only the binary, a LICENSE and four fonts. Panel lettering came from the VCV library screenshot at https://library.vcvrack.com/screenshots/400/DigitalAtavism/Blip.png because the plugin ships no panel SVG at all — the panels are drawn at runtime by Blip::Widget::draw. Parameter 3 is configured by the count passed to config() but never given a configParam or a ParamWidget, so it has no name, no tooltip and no position, and cannot be clicked; outputs 0 and 1 are the same, leftovers of the shared layout with Coin. The oscillator runs at eight times the engine rate and the eight sub-samples are averaged. The trigger threshold is Rack's usual rescale of 0.1 to 2.0 volts. The envelope has two timed stages, hold then release; the hold stage adds a punch term, which on this module is stored as zero, so the hold is flat.

Coin.notes: No published source; read from the installed 2.0.0 plugin.dylib, which is unstripped. THE PUNCH KNOB'S DEFAULT IS OUTSIDE ITS OWN RANGE. Coin's constructor at +0x9340 calls configParam for parameter 3 with a minimum of 0.3, a maximum of 0.6 and a default of 1.0; Rack does not clamp a default, so the knob comes up at 100% while its tooltip range reads 30% to 60%, and Initialise puts it back there. The punch term is used at +0xa278 as an extra envelope level of one plus twice the remaining hold fraction times the punch, so at the default it starts the note three times over full scale and the output clips for the first part of the hold. Output 0 is configured by the count passed to config() but has no configOutput and no PortWidget, so it cannot be clicked or patched; it is a leftover of the layout shared with Blip and Hit. The oscillator is a plain 50% square wave with no pulse-width or waveform control, oversampled eight times. The panel prints TRIG twice, on the pitch-change output near the top and on the note input at the bottom. Panel lettering came from https://library.vcvrack.com/screenshots/400/DigitalAtavism/Coin.png; the plugin ships no panel SVG.

DTrig.notes: No published source; read from the installed 2.0.0 plugin.dylib, which is unstripped. The knob figures come from the constructor at +0xc294 and +0xc318: delay 0.0015 to 2 seconds with a default of 0.15, gate 0.001 to 1 second with a default of 0.001, both shown in ms by a display multiplier of 1000. So the gate knob comes up at its own minimum, a 1ms pulse. Each of the two CV jacks is a multiplier on its knob through exp2f, so a patched cable resting at 0V leaves the knob alone; the delay result is capped at 5 seconds and the gate at 5 seconds with a 1ms floor, both above what the knobs alone can reach. The write-back at +0xc880 and +0xc940 is a maximum rather than an assignment, which is why a retrigger cannot shorten a delay already in progress. The panel prints DLAY and TIME beside the jack-and-knob pairs and TRIG twice, once on the input and once on the output; the maker's tooltips for the second pair are Gate time on the knob and Gate length on the jack. Panel lettering came from https://library.vcvrack.com/screenshots/400/DigitalAtavism/DTrig.png; the plugin ships no panel SVG.

Hit.notes: No published source; read from the installed 2.0.0 plugin.dylib, which is unstripped. THE LOW-PASS FILTER IS SHUT BY DEFAULT. The constructor at +0xdab8 configures parameter 7, the knob the panel prints LPF, from 0 to 1 with a default of 0. Hit::process +0xe6ec turns it into a filter coefficient of 0.1 times the cube of 0.9 times the knob plus 0.1, so a knob at 0 gives 0.0001 and a knob at 1 gives 0.1. The filter at +0xed70 is applied on every sub-sample with no bypass, so at the default the corner is far below the audio band and the module is effectively silent until LPF is raised. The HPF knob, parameter 6, is squared and scaled by 0.1 at +0xe71c and is genuinely out of the path at 0. Index order is not panel order for these two: parameter 7 (LPF) sits above parameter 6 (HPF) on the panel, at census positions 90,270 and 90,300, and they are tagged accordingly. Neither filter has a CV jack. The noise source is a fresh rand() value taken thirty-two times per oscillator cycle, so it is pitched rather than white. The pitch bend multiplies the oscillator period once per sample by one plus a hundredth of the cube of the setting, and the period is held between 8 and 400000 samples. Panel lettering came from https://library.vcvrack.com/screenshots/400/DigitalAtavism/Hit.png; the plugin ships no panel SVG.

UT-P.notes: No published source; read from the installed 2.0.0 plugin.dylib, which is unstripped. The selector maths is at +0x10a9c: the CV is rescaled from the chosen voltage range onto 0 to 1, multiplied by the number of channels less one, has 0.5 added and is truncated, then clamped, so each channel occupies an equal slice of the range and the boundaries fall half way between. The voltage range is a module setting, not a per-jack one, and it is saved with the patch under the key voltageRange; the seven names are spelled exactly as listed, from DigitalAtavism::VoltageRange::GetName, and the limits come from the tables beside it: 0 to 10, 0 to 5, 0 to 1, -10 to 10, -5 to 5, -2.5 to 2.5 and -1 to 1. A new module comes up on the first of them, set by the constructor at +0x10350. The menu item itself is labelled Voltage Range: followed by the current choice, and opens a submenu. Two lights are declared in the call to config() and neither is given a LightWidget or ever written, so nothing on the panel shows them. IN and CV behave differently from each other: a polyphonic CV drives a per-channel switch, while a mono CV places the chosen value on the output channel matching the chosen position rather than on channel 1. No family is given to IN or OUT because they carry whatever is sent through them. Panel lettering came from https://library.vcvrack.com/screenshots/400/DigitalAtavism/UT-P.png; the plugin ships no panel SVG.

UT-OX.notes: No published source; read from the installed 2.0.0 plugin.dylib, which is unstripped. UT_OX::process +0x124c4 checks that the left neighbour's model is UT-P or UT-OX before reading its expander message, so a chain of them all work from the one polyphonic input; +0x1263c then passes the same message on to the right, but only when the module there is a UT-OX. WITH NO VALID NEIGHBOUR IT DOES NOT FALL SILENT IN THE OBVIOUS WAY. The fallback at +0x12560 builds a message of sixteen zero values, so the selector still moves across sixteen positions and the trigger output still fires as the CV is swept, while the signal output stays at 0V. Unlike UT-P this module is mono throughout: the CV jack is read at channel one only and both outputs are single-channel. The voltage range menu is the same one UT-P carries, from the shared UT_Base::BaseWidget, saved under the key voltageRange and starting at 0V - 10V. The panel has no IN jack and no GATE output. Panel lettering came from https://library.vcvrack.com/screenshots/400/DigitalAtavism/UT-OX.png; the plugin ships no panel SVG.
